profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit AI research organization founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, Washington. It is currently led by Ali Farhadi. The organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering aimed at tackling key problems in artificial intelligence, with a stated emphasis on open, collaborative, and inclusive principles intended to produce safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. Its research extends into applied areas including climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection. Ai2 maintains partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the National Science Foundation on an open multimodal AI infrastructure project, and Google Cloud to support model development and environmental modeling platforms.

Ai2's primary AI products include OLMo, an open-source language model developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, and Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs with a nonprofit research focus. Both products reflect the organization's commitment to openness in AI development rather than commercial deployment.

The site's held facts indicate that Ai2 has a notable legal exposure footprint in Washington state, with 47 associated entries recorded there, though no specific litigation cases are listed in the available data.
